definition: Trepidation means nervous fear or uneasy apprehension about what is coming.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word trepidation. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know trepidation should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: She saved the voicemail for two days, playing everything else first, and pressed it at last with trepidation.
Unease is milder than trepidation — a low hum that something is off while you keep working; trepidation shakes in the body but still proceeds.
Terror goes further than trepidation — trepidation trembles and proceeds; terror has stopped proceeding altogether.

Apprehension is worry about what is coming — flat, mental, and containable; you can list your fears in an even voice. Trepidation is the same forward-looking fear with the body joined in: the tremble, the held breath, the stomach that drops. Apprehension sits in the head; trepidation shakes the hands.

The jitters are the informal, bodily name for pre-event nerves — bouncing knees before a recital, restless hands before an interview. Trepidation is the polished, formal word for the same trembling fear, the one that fits a written sentence. Same shaking; the register is the whole difference.
nerves held steady
boldness where fear would be

Latin trepidare, 'to tremble,' survives in exactly one other common English word: intrepid, the fearless one who does not tremble — and this course teaches intrepid on its own card. Beyond that pair the root went quiet, so learn trepidation directly: fear with a tremble in it.

Trepidation is the exact word for that morning, because trepidation means fear or nervous apprehension — from Latin trepidare, to tremble: fear you can feel in your body while your head insists everything is fine.
Panic has lost the argument entirely; trepidation still walks to the board, it just holds its breath on the way.
Trepidation is the polished word for stage-fright-grade nerves, often with a wry smile: with some trepidation, I opened the email.
Apprehension is flatter; dread is heavier and surer of doom.
